groups.core-model: Structures, forests, rows and items: the hierarchy model and its storage-facing managers
groups.generators: Automation that builds or reshapes a forest: inserters, extenders, groupers, sorters, filters
groups.attributes: Values shown in columns and used by formulas: loaders, aggregates, expressions
groups.effects: Write-back from structure changes or attribute values to Jira (effect providers, effectors)
groups.sync: Synchronizers keeping a structure and Jira data (links, sub-tasks, Agile, filters) in step
groups.query: Structured JQL (S-JQL), the structure() JQL function and query constraints
groups.views-columns: Saved views, column definitions, notes columns
groups.persistence: Database tables (Active Objects), properties, locks and stored settings
groups.history-events: Change tracking, issue events, structure history and activity streams
groups.permissions-security: Structure permissions, access checks and security filters
groups.jobs-processes: Background jobs and long-running user processes with progress
groups.export: Export and print renderers (Excel, printable view, JSON)
groups.integrations: Integrations with other apps (Agile, Advanced Roadmaps, Tempo, Assets/Insight, Service Management, ScriptRunner and others)
groups.ui-pages: Front-end resources and server-rendered pages: board, grid, dialogs, admin pages
groups.ui-navigation: Menus, web sections and items, web panels, keyboard shortcut
groups.admin-config: Global and per-project configuration and defaults
groups.licensing-support: Licensing, end-of-life notices, support tools, statistics
groups.platform: Jira-version adaptation, lifecycle, caching, cluster and utility services
groups.cfd: Cumulative flow diagram gadget and its back end
groups.extension-points: Module types and services the plugin offers to companion apps
groups.user-data: User key changes, anonymisation and ownership transfer (GDPR)

modules.purpose: Single public entry point exported to other plugins that hands out the main Structure services (structure, row, forest, attribute, generator, folder, view, favorite, sync, job, backup, effector, property and query services).
Stores and answers which license serial numbers the vendor's app-support check has marked as blocked; other modules and extension apps query it to restrict licensed functionality.

Public background job manager with named thread pools: user (3), indexing (2), system (1), and generator, attribute and effector pools sized by configuration. Jobs run with the submitting user's identity and can be queried or cancelled.

Public service to create and track long-running processes (e.g. copying, maintenance, effector runs): issues handles for progress reporting, user-visible status and cancellation, with caching; backs the Processes page and process REST.
Public service that creates backup, restore (current backup format), migrate and migrate-preview operations for Structure data.

Holds the app's global and per-user configuration: which projects Structure is enabled for, app permissions (use, create structure, synchronization, automation, configure generators/effectors, execute effectors, manage global saved columns) as 'anyone' flags or subject lists, default structure globally and per project, issue/project page UI defaults and per-user overrides, and attribute sensitivity settings.

Public issue event bridge: listens to Jira issue, issue-link, remote-link and issue-property events and redistributes them to Structure's issue listeners; also lets other code report issue changes explicitly.

Stores which structures each user marked as favorite and computes structure popularity (number of users who favorited it); lists a user's favorites (optionally including archived), sorts and filters structures by popularity, removes entries for vanished users or structures, and deletes a user's favorites on anonymization.

Public view service; on first use (cluster-locked) creates the default views 'Issue Details', 'Basic view', 'Planning', 'Tracking', 'Triage', 'Entry' and 'Gadget View', reusing same-named existing ones, and sets them as the global default view settings per page; otherwise delegates to the stored view manager.
Public factory for building S-JQL structure queries programmatically.
Public parser turning S-JQL text into executable structure queries over a forest, using registered constraints.

Public row service unifying persistent and transient rows: resolves rows by id, scans many rows, creates rows, finds all rows for an item, and builds row mappers that trace generated rows back to their originals.

Public attribute service: loads values of attributes (fields, formulas, aggregates, progress, etc.) for rows of a forest or for items, in bulk, with consistency checks against forest changes, update checking and per-user security; used by the grid, REST, export and gadgets.

Public service for creating, retrieving and dropping attribute subscriptions, which keep a set of attribute values for a forest loaded in the background and report incremental value changes to clients; idle subscriptions expire.

Central store of structures and their forests: creates, copies (with or without forest), restores, archives and deletes structures; enforces permission levels (view, edit, admin) and generator/effector configuration rights; persists forests and forest change logs, records history, keeps the issue index current, publishes structure-deleted events, and periodically trims stored forest changes.

Public generator service: creates, updates, deletes and looks up generators, routing to the persistent store or the in-memory transient store by id, resolves a generator spec to its extension module, and records changes for tracking.

Public service that turns item identities into the actual objects (issues, projects, users, generic items, etc.) by delegating to the registered item types, in bulk where supported, checking visibility for the current user and returning nothing for unknown or inaccessible items.
Public store of folder items (name and owning structure) used to group rows in a structure, with caching and change tracking.

Manages synchronizer instances attached to structures: install, update, uninstall, enable/disable autosync, full and one-time resync (as background processes), ownership transfer. Listens to issue and structure changes and runs incremental synchronization roughly every 2 seconds with throttling, sending email on sync errors; stores definitions in the database.

Records an audit trail of synchronizer actions: each sync run writes a description record plus action records grouped together, buffered and written to the database every 30 seconds; supports querying by synchronizer, structure and time range (capped) and deleting records older than a date. Shown in the admin support pages.

Public general-purpose helper service: fetches issues with permission and project-enablement checks, checks Structure app permissions and admin rights, runs JQL searches and issue matching, lists visible projects, groups and roles, and requires the plugin's web resources (widget, issue details, quick edit) on pages.

Public service that runs registered periodic jobs: about once a minute it checks each job, takes a cluster lock, decides if it should run and executes it on the system job pool, recording the last run time in plugin properties. Jobs can be added, removed or forced to run.
Public global key/value store for plugin settings and state (strings, booleans, longs), cached without expiry and cluster-aware.

Public per-structure key/value store (keys up to 170 characters) used for structure-level settings such as quick transformations, description visibility, manual adjustments flag and last-used time; supports bulk reads across structures.

Public change-tracking service: other modules record that items changed and consumers ask for all changed items since a data version. On a single node it is in-memory; on Data Center changes are written to a shared table so all nodes see them, and issue reindex activity is taken into account.

Public service that resolves a forest specification (stored structure, query, transformed or secured view, clipboard) to a live forest source, applying generators and transformations, caching sources, and naming forests for display.

Public validated create/update/delete service for generic items. Checks licence, that the user may use Structure, that the user is not anonymous for creation, item existence, and edit permission on the owning structure before delegating to the generic item manager; returns validation results with errors.

Public store for 'generic items' (memos, planning tasks and other plugin-defined item types): creates, reads, updates, deletes and restores them in the database, caches them, records an audit history entry on every change and notifies the item tracker. Items may be owned by a structure, in which case visibility follows that structure's view permission.

Persists and serves the change history of generic items: one record per create or update with old and new name, description and parameters, author and timestamp. Records are cached and can be queried per item in time order; this feeds the memo change-history view.
Public in-memory store of effect batches (pending changes produced by generator actions) for a user, identified by node-specific ids and discarded after about 71 seconds.

Collects anonymous usage statistics: components record counts and active users asynchronously; pending values are flushed to the database every 10 minutes. A daily job purges old data and, if the admin opted in, posts the aggregated report to the vendor's app-support endpoint. Also decides whether to show the 'enable statistics' offer and remembers dismissals.

Public service that runs effectors (automation that writes changes back to Jira): validates permissions, starts processes for a structure's effector instances or a one-off effector, supports preview and confirmation, applying, cancelling, undo, resume of interrupted runs and acknowledgement; one node applies at a time in Data Center.
Public store of configured effector instances (an effector module key, its parameters and owning structure), with create, restore, read, update and delete and caching.
Public service giving typed access to memo items (lightweight text items placed in structures) by id: read one or many memos and get an update builder for their fields.
Public service giving typed access to planning-task items (issue-like placeholders that can later become issues) by id: read one or many and get an update builder for their fields.

modules.name: module-type:structure-synchronizer
modules.purpose: Declares the synchronizer extension point: modules of this kind (with label, description, rules text, order and a configuration form template) become selectable synchronizers that can be installed on a structure to keep it in sync with Jira data.

modules.name: module-type:structure-export-renderer-provider
modules.purpose: Declares the export renderer provider extension point: modules supply renderers that turn column values into cells when a structure is exported to Excel or printed.

modules.name: module-type:structure-item-type
modules.purpose: Declares the item type extension point: each module defines a kind of item that can be placed in structure rows (issues, folders, memos, Jira objects, etc.), how it is resolved, displayed, checked for visibility, created or edited.

modules.name: module-type:structure-inserter
modules.purpose: Declares the inserter generator extension point: modules add a list of items at the generator position when a structure is built; each has a label, dialog title, icon, configuration form and summary template.

modules.name: module-type:structure-extender
modules.purpose: Declares the extender generator extension point: modules add child items under existing items (e.g. sub-tasks, linked issues) at configured levels when the forest is generated.

modules.name: module-type:structure-grouper
modules.purpose: Declares the grouper generator extension point: modules insert group rows and place items under the group matching a computed value, optionally changing item data when rows are moved between groups.

modules.name: module-type:structure-filter
modules.purpose: Declares the filter generator extension point: modules hide rows in the generated forest that do not satisfy a condition.

modules.name: module-type:structure-sorter
modules.purpose: Declares the sorter generator extension point: modules reorder sibling rows by a value, optionally turning manual reordering into data changes (such as rank).

modules.name: module-type:structure-attribute-loader-provider
modules.purpose: Declares the attribute loader provider extension point: modules contribute loaders that compute attribute values (fields, aggregates, formulas) for rows shown in structure columns, exports and queries.

modules.name: module-type:new-structure-template
modules.purpose: Declares the new structure template extension point: each module appears as a choice in the Create Structure wizard, with title, description, icon and step templates, and configures the newly created structure.

modules.name: module-type:structure-query-constraint
modules.purpose: Declares the S-JQL constraint extension point: each module registers a named constraint function (attribute fname) that can be used inside S-JQL queries to match rows.

modules.name: module-type:structure-effector
modules.purpose: Declares the effector extension point: effectors compute a set of Jira changes (effects) from structure contents and attribute values that users can preview and apply, with a configuration form and summary template.

modules.name: module-type:structure-core-extension
modules.purpose: Declares a generic internal extension point through which add-ons can contribute configuration to the structure widget and attach extra data to structure REST responses (poll, forest, item, effect).

modules.name: module-type:structure-performance-log-provider
modules.purpose: Declares the performance log provider extension point: modules contribute named sections of diagnostic performance information shown in the plugin's performance/troubleshooting output.

modules.name: module-type:structure-query-skeleton-factory
modules.purpose: Declares an extension point that lets add-ons turn a typed search query (e.g. a Confluence CQL query) into an initial forest skeleton for an ad-hoc search structure; JQL and text query types are handled internally by built-in inserters.

modules.name: module-type:structure-effect-provider
modules.purpose: Declares the effect provider extension point: modules know how to describe, apply and undo a specific kind of Jira change (field value, status, comment, conversion) that generators and effectors request.

modules.name: module-type:structure-backup-provider
modules.purpose: Declares an extension point through which add-ons participate in Structure backup, restore and migration, writing and reading their own data for the selected structures.

modules.name: module-type:structure-calendar-provider
modules.purpose: Declares the calendar provider extension point: modules list work calendars (by numeric id and name) that formulas and duration calculations can use.

modules.name: module-type:structure-integration-details-provider
modules.purpose: Declares an extension point for companion add-ons to report a product icon and which structures they integrate with, so Structure can show integration markers on its structure lists.

modules.name: rest:REST API 1.0
modules.purpose: Registers the older Structure REST API version 1.0 used by the structure board, gadgets and admin pages: configuration lookups, field configuration, gadget metadata, perspectives (shareable view state), S-JQL troubleshooting, usage statistics, UI configuration, views and widget configuration.

modules.name: rest:REST API 2.0
modules.purpose: Registers the main Structure REST API version 2.0 used by the structure grid and other UIs: structures, forests and updates, polling, attribute values and subscriptions, items, generation control, effects and effector processes, history, notes, saved columns, pickers, configuration and permissions, and miscellaneous helpers.

modules.name: rest:REST CFD API 1.0
modules.purpose: Registers the REST API of the bundled Cumulative Flow Diagram gadget: gadget metadata and validation, feature status, and forecast simulation of a CFD.

Core extension used by the Structure dashboard gadget: when a REST response is assembled it accepts the gadget's requested row windows (forest, row indexes, attributes) and creates attribute value subscriptions for them, returning the subscriptions and a mapping from old to new subscription ids.
Provides cluster-aware caches (expiring and non-expiring, via Jira's cache manager), node-local caches and cluster locks to all plugin components.

Runs Structure database maintenance (backup, cleanup of orphaned forests, views, perspectives, favourites and properties, removal of old history, sync audit, processes and backups, reindexing) manually or on a daily-time or cron schedule (default 03:00), under a cluster-wide lock, reporting progress through a process.

Persists usage statistics samples (timestamp, user key, statistic name, value) in the database, answers unique-user counts per statistic over a time range, builds a report from samples since a timestamp, deletes old samples, and participates in user anonymization and user-key rename by counting and rewriting a user's records.
Assembles the 'Performance Audit Log' tree from all registered performance-log provider modules, isolating failures; shown on the admin performance audit page and used for support diagnostics.

Contributes feature-usage counters to the statistics report by scanning all structures (as system): number of automated structures and generators by module key (with field or attribute detail for some), effector instances, folders, memos by icon, planning tasks, and synchronizers per module and enabled state.

Persists long-running process records: status, timestamp, display parameters, managing user, current activity, percent complete and cancellation flag; supports update, delete and bulk deletion of old processes.
At startup verifies that Structure's Active Objects tables are usable; if initialisation fails it shuts the Structure plugin down with a prominent log message unless an override flag is set.

Runs Jira issue index searches for Structure: executes JQL or parsed queries (optionally sorted), matches a list of issues against a query in chunks, reads index field values for issue sets, and refuses search when a full reindex is running or the index is inconsistent. Periodically clears Jira's JQL literals cache to limit memory.

Protects Structure index searches and synchronization from Jira's full lock-down reindex: waits for the index lock, detects running reindex via events, reports when index use is impossible or the consistency check failed, and retries on closed readers.

Version-specific adapter for searching Jira's issue index: returns matching issue ids, streams ids or single/multi field values for a query and user, exposes the max clause count and doc-values reading.
Clears Jira's thread-local index searchers so later searches see fresh index data; Jira-version-specific.

Computes a user's access level (none, view, edit, automation, control/admin) to a structure or view from its owner, ordered permission rules (users, groups, project roles, everyone, inheritance from another structure), Jira admin status and global Structure settings, and evaluates global app permissions (use, create structures, synchronization, automation, generators, effectors, global saved columns).
Short-term cache of computed structure permission levels per user and of global app-permission checks, cleared periodically and on all cluster nodes via a cluster message when permissions change.

Controls the start and stop of all Structure components with the plugin lifecycle: logs a start banner with version, instance id and licence summary, enables cache clearing, subscribes to Jira shutdown, and cleans up leaked thread-locals and template caches on stop.

Public utility that periodically calls registered subjects at their requested periods from a single low-priority daemon thread, stopping the thread when idle; used for heartbeat and housekeeping tasks.

Watches the Jira Software and Jira Service Management plugins; when they are installed, upgraded or removed it refreshes and restarts Structure so its optional integrations rewire, recording a flag to avoid repeated refreshes at startup.

Saves and loads perspectives for licensed users who can use Structure, validating the spec, applying saved-column updates to the embedded view specs on load, deleting stale ones for maintenance, and reporting perspective count statistics.

Stores perspectives (saved snapshots of the Structure page state used for shareable links) with random ids, updates last-used time on read, deletes those unused since a cutoff, counts and restores them.
Inserter generator that adds the user's recently viewed issues (Jira issue history, most recent first) and refreshes them about once a minute.

Stores views (named column/layout specifications with owner, permissions and sharing) and per-structure view settings (which views are offered and default per page: board, issue page, project tab, gadget) plus global defaults; enforces view creation and sharing rights, builds view menus, and reports pinned-column statistics.

Listens to issue updates; when the Sprint field of an issue changes, it reports a synthetic 'sprint updated' change for each of that issue's sub-tasks so structures and attributes depending on inherited sprint refresh.

Event queue feeding synchronizers: records Jira changes, structure history entries, resync requests and autosync-enable notices, and hands them to the sync manager in batches. On a single node it keeps events in memory; on Data Center it shares them through the database across nodes, optionally postponing while issues are being reindexed.
Stores the manual order of items kept by a manual sorter generator, one record per generator and parent path, as a comma-separated list of serialized item ids.

Short-lived cache (about 5 minutes) of rendered HTML image tags for Jira issue constants (issue type, priority, status, resolution) per locale, making relative icon URLs absolute. Used when rendering cells and exports.
Short-lived cache of interactive HTML avatars for users (small avatar with user hover card markup), falling back to the anonymous avatar, used in the grid UI.
Same as the user avatar cache but renders plain image tags (name and display name as alt/title) suitable for printable and exported output.
Maintains the lookup of S-JQL constraint names from all enabled S-JQL constraint modules, rebuilt when the module set changes and warning on name conflicts.
S-JQL constraint 'item' that matches rows by item type (standard short names or full module keys, '*' for all) and optionally by text or regular expression on the item's display text.
Bundle of Jira services (time zones, i18n, time-tracking configuration, date-time formatter factory, extension registry) made available to formula functions at evaluation time.

Parses and analyzes formula-language (Expr) expressions: prepares executors, reports syntax errors with expected tokens, lists variables and dependencies, and lists the available functions and aggregations with canonical names.

Supplies the formula language's standard function library (logic, comparison, arithmetic, rounding, math, text, regex, date and time, user, field and Jira entity lookups) with aliases and documentation links.

Supplies the formula language's aggregate functions over a row's subtree or other scopes (sum, count, min, max, average, median, percentile, quartile, join, array, unique min/max) with documentation links.
Holds the limit on array size in formula (Expr) evaluation, read from configuration.
Static access point to standard Jira services (authentication context, project, component, version, constants, options, user managers, OSGi lookups) for code that cannot receive them by injection.

Converts arbitrary issue field values (including values from third-party custom fields such as Advanced Roadmaps team and Tree custom field) into display text, joining multiple values with commas; used for text attributes, grouping, export and field information.
Tracks running generations of automated forests per forest specification, can block regeneration, and enforces generation time limits (global default 30 s, per-structure override, hard maximum).

Stores per-structure, per-item text properties (used for the Notes columns): one value per structure, item and property name, cached and invalidated on change; also lists or deletes all properties of a structure. Changing a value marks the item as changed.

Resolves an editor for an item property name: the built-in default 'notes' property or a stored note ('dc_note_<n>'), so the item update REST call can edit note cells with permission checks and archived-note protection.

Persists effector process state and effect records: process status transitions, preview, timestamps, owning user and node, and per-effect records with undo data; caches processes and running processes per user.
Bounded, slowly expiring cache that remembers the resolved loader for each attribute specification so repeated attribute requests skip loader resolution.

Decides which attributes are treated as sensitive (may leak data from items the user cannot see) according to the admin's security setting: standard, strict or permissive, plus an admin whitelist of non-sensitive attributes.
Coordinates attribute-loading processes with cache clearing: running loads are cancelled when caches are cleared or the plugin stops, and new loads wait until a clear completes.

Owns the shared attribute value cache and its change observer and loading protector, wiring them to the row manager, item tracker and forest service so attribute values are invalidated when items or forests change.
Builds a diagnostic dump of the attribute subsystem (historical timing statistics, broken attributes, cache size by attribute) shown on the admin attribute troubleshooting page.
Background worker that periodically evicts old generations of cached attribute values when the cache grows too large, reporting removed and retained counts to performance statistics.
Caches Jira-wide configuration lookups (default locale, set of navigable field ids) and clears them on general configuration change events and every 5 minutes.
Records when each structure was last used (polled), throttled to at most one write per structure every two hours, so 'Manage structures' can show last-used dates.
Installs and clears a fake current HTTP request on non-request threads so Jira code that expects one works in background jobs; Jira-version-specific (javax/jakarta).
Version-specific factory for the Jira helper objects used when evaluating web fragments (request, optional project and context parameters).

Creates a per-thread Jira environment for background jobs: prepares Jira's thread-local state and, unless disabled, installs an emulated HTTP request (with the base URL's context path) so request-dependent Jira code works; cleans up afterwards.

Maintains a database index of which issues occur in which structures (with occurrence counts), updated incrementally when structure content changes and rebuilt per structure on reindex; answers 'is issue X in structure Y' and 'which structures contain issue X' using a cache keyed by issue.

Loads the delivery scope and training history for the CFD feature, groups stories and epics by team, derives averages such as stories per epic, and drives the per-team completion simulator; also records a calculation trace for diagnostics.

Reads a structure's forest as an agile delivery hierarchy for the CFD feature: identifies epics and stories by configured issue types, and reads each story's key, team (default 'No Team'), status category (to do / in progress / done) and appearance, start and completion dates via attributes.
Supplies the random integer distribution (geometric, parameterised by a mean) used by the CFD completion simulation to sample how many stories or how much throughput occurs per interval.

Computes the predictive cumulative flow diagram: loads historical delivery from a training structure and remaining work from a scope structure, builds per-team throughput models and runs a Monte-Carlo style completion simulation, returning past and predicted flow series, per-team statistics and predicted completion dates; refuses when the feature is disabled.

Validates the settings of the Cumulative Flow Diagram gadget (scope and training structures, training period, team and completion attributes, issue types, target date, ignore threshold) and returns per-field localized errors, the scope and training structures and the current user; also reports whether the predictive CFD feature is enabled.

modules.name: servlet-filter:End of Life Decorator
modules.purpose: Runs before page decoration on the Jira dashboard, admin pages, Structure admin pages and the Structure Board. For Jira administrators only, if the Structure license or its maintenance (or that of a bundled extension app) has expired or expires soon, it adds the end-of-life banner resource to the page.

modules.name: servlet-filter:Enable Statistics Offer Decorator
modules.purpose: On the admin summary, admin pages and Structure admin pages, when the viewer is a Jira system administrator who should still be offered usage statistics sending, adds the statistics-offer banner resource asking them to enable anonymous statistics.

modules.name: servlet-filter:Issue Change Interceptor
modules.purpose: Wraps Jira requests that change issues without firing normal issue events: Agile ranking, sub-task reordering, voting/watching and watcher REST calls, Agile epic add/remove and the sub-task move REST call. It gathers affected issue ids or keys (parameters, URL or captured JSON body) and afterwards reports them to Structure's change tracking as rank, reorder or update changes.

modules.name: servlet-filter:Bulk Change Interceptor
modules.purpose: Supports Jira bulk change started from Structure. On /secure/Bulk* pages, if the session holds a Structure-created bulk-edit selection, it substitutes that selection's search into the session, redirects the final return to the issue navigator back to the originating Structure page, and keeps Structure's selected issues when Jira replaces the bulk-edit state.

modules.name: servlet-filter:Plugin Manager Helper
modules.purpose: On the Universal Plugin Manager pages, if Structure or a bundled extension app is licensed through a vendor-provided or bundled license (not a Marketplace license), it adds the plugin-manager helper resource that annotates the UPM listing and points to Structure's own license page.

modules.name: servlet-filter:Tempo Internal Issues Interceptor
modules.purpose: Watches PUT requests to Tempo's internal issue REST endpoints (which modify issues without normal Jira events). It resolves the issue key from the URL and, after the request completes, reports an issue-updated change to Structure's change tracking so attributes and generated content refresh.

modules.name: servlet-filter:Security Filter for external gadget
modules.purpose: Runs before login on the external (embeddable) Structure gadget page. It intercepts the Content-Security-Policy header Jira sets and replaces it with a policy computed by a shared security helper that is aware of application links, so the page can be framed by linked applications such as Confluence.

modules.name: servlet-filter: Partitioned Cookie Header Filter
modules.purpose: For HTTPS POST requests to the external gadget page (login form) and to the authenticate REST call when s_partitioned=true, adds Secure, SameSite=None and Partitioned attributes to the session cookies set in the response, so logging in inside a third-party iframe (e.g. a Confluence macro) works in browsers with partitioned cookies.

Determines Structure's effective licence from all sources (Marketplace/UPM licence, a legacy licence key stored in Jira application properties, bundled or app-support data), exposes licensed / writable checks, and allows installing or removing the legacy licence.

modules.name: web-panel:GreenHopper tab
modules.purpose: Adds a 'Structure' tab to the issue detail view on Jira Software (Agile) boards. It renders an empty container that the Agile-board script fills with a structure widget anchored on the selected issue. Shown only if Structure is enabled for issue pages, the user may use Structure, the issue's project is enabled and non-archived structures exist.

modules.name: issue-page:Structure Helper Panel
modules.purpose: Hidden data panel in the right column of the Jira issue view. It emits the issue id/key and flags (show Structure section, issue not in the initially selected structure, auto-collapse, navigation hint used, show time tracking) that the issue-page script reads to build the Structure section and Structure time-tracking.

modules.name: issue-page:Structure on Issue Page
modules.purpose: Placeholder 'Structure' module in the left column of the Jira issue view. Its own content is empty; the issue-page script replaces it with a structure widget showing structures that contain the issue (with recent, favorite and default structure choices). Displayed when Structure is enabled for issue pages and the user has access to non-archived structures.

modules.name: project-navigation:Structure web item
modules.purpose: Adds a 'Structure' entry to the project sidebar navigation. It opens the project page with the Structure panel selected, shown only when the user may use Structure and the project is enabled for Structure.

Content of the project sidebar 'Structure' page: a Structure Board widget scoped to the current project (project key, id and a project scope name passed as hidden fields), with a toolbar and issue action links. Loads the widget resources and the project-page script; shows an error message if one is set.

modules.name: web-resource:Project Page Resources
modules.purpose: Script for the project sidebar Structure page: wires the project-scoped structure widget, its page settings dialog and link to the project's Structure settings.

modules.name: menu:Structure
modules.purpose: The 'Structure' entry in Jira's top navigation bar, opening the Structure Board. It is also the dropdown that holds the welcome, recent, favorite, default, query, management and effector sections. Shown to users allowed to use Structure.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Welcome to Structure Section
modules.purpose: Section of the Structure top menu that holds the 'Welcome to Structure' link. Shown unless the welcome feature has been switched off by a dark feature.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Welcome to Structure
modules.purpose: Menu link 'Welcome to Structure' that opens the Structure welcome page.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Recent Structures Section
modules.purpose: 'Recent Structures' section of the Structure top menu. Shown when the user can see at least one non-archived structure; filled by the recent-structures link factory.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Favorite Structures
modules.purpose: 'Favorite Structures' section of the Structure top menu. Shown only when the user has favorite structures; filled by the favorites link factory.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Default Structures Section
modules.purpose: 'Default Structure' section of the Structure top menu. Shown when the system-wide default structure, or the default structure of the current project, is viewable by the user.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Default Project Structure
modules.purpose: Menu link to the current project's default structure, labelled with the abbreviated structure name and the project key. Shown only when that structure is viewable and differs from the system default.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Default System Structure
modules.purpose: Menu link to the system-wide default structure, labelled with its abbreviated name and its description as tooltip. Shown when that structure is viewable.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Recent Structures Factory
modules.purpose: Lazily builds the 'Recent Structures' menu links: the user's recently viewed structures first, then other viewable structures ordered by popularity, up to half of Jira's dropdown limit (at least four). Each link opens the board for that structure, with the name shortened to 40 characters.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Favorite Structures Factory
modules.purpose: Lazily builds the 'Favorite Structures' menu links from the user's favorites, up to half of Jira's dropdown limit (at least four). If there are more, it adds a 'more' link to the favorites view of Manage Structures.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Open Query Section
modules.purpose: Section of the Structure top menu that holds the 'Query' link.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Query
modules.purpose: Menu link 'Query' that opens the Structure Board in query mode with an empty JQL search, so issues can be searched and shown in the board.

modules.name: menu:Structure|Structure Management
modules.purpose: Section of the Structure top menu holding 'Create Structure' and 'Manage Structures'.

Creates and deletes many issue links in one transaction for a user, choosing either a direct entity-store implementation or Jira's link manager depending on a flag; used by link synchronizers and effectors.

Persistent mapping between item type keys (complete plugin module keys of item types) and compact integer ids used in other tables. Preloads and caches all registrations and creates new ones optimistically with retries under concurrency.
Provides the plugin's direct database access (connections, SQL with resolved table names) on top of Active Objects for the Structure plugin key.

Plugin-wide database lock used while the whole Structure database is replaced or migrated (for example restore): sets a 'locked' flag in the BOOTSTRAP table that every cluster node sees, so other database work is refused until it is unlocked by the locking thread or by a forced unlock; waits up to a configurable timeout (60 s default).

Shared database access layer over Active Objects for all plugin tables: find, count, create (also with explicit id), delete, raw SQL with table/column substitution, sorted/limited queries and a small where-clause builder, respecting the database lock state and a 999-parameter batch limit.

In-memory bidirectional mapping of item identities to compact integer codes: issues map to their positive id, other items get negative codes assigned on demand. Used for memory-efficient transient rows.

Stores persistent rows: each row id maps to an item (type, numeric or string id) and semantics. Creates and restores rows, scans rows in bulk with caching, and finds rows for an item through reverse caches.
Keeps in memory the temporary rows created by generators (each tied to its creator and original row), with compact item encoding and per-creator indexes; rows are cleaned when creators drop them.
Keeps short-lived generator instances (for example those created for query or transformation views) in memory, assigning them ids distinguishable from persistent ones.
Stores persistent generator instances (generator module key, parameters, owning structure) in the database with caching; supports restoring with a given id during backup restore.
Public cache answering which rows, issues and items of a forest are invisible to a given user, checking issue visibility via Jira search and other item types via their own access checks.
Public cache answering which issues belong to projects where Structure is not enabled, using the indexed project of each issue and the plugin's project configuration.
Public cache answering which issues are sub-tasks, based on the indexed issue type.
Forwards every issue change reported by the issue event bridge to the item tracker so that cached forests and attribute values for those issues are refreshed.

Collects forest changes during structure updates and commits them as versioned history entries (with user and synchronizer), supporting batches, cancellation, restoring entries from backup, clearing history for a structure or version range, batch listeners, anonymization counts and user-key renames.

Database writer for structure change history: writes a history entry (previous version, timestamp, user, synchronizer) with its forest changes (operation, moved forest, source/target paths and positions, direction, original rows), writes issue and project index rows per entry, deletes ranges of history, counts and renames user keys.

Read side of structure history: returns history entries for a structure between versions, latest version, entry counts (optionally since a date), reconstructs a forest as of a past version, and runs activity queries (by structures, issues, projects, users, time) with limits for activity streams and the history REST API.

Decides what the Structure panel shows when opened on the board, issue or project page: applies the user's UI settings and auto-switch strategy, resolves the default structure (skipping archived ones), and picks the initial structure: the only viewable one, an explicitly requested one, the one remembered from navigation for the same issue, then the strategy's choice.

Bulk-clones a set of issues (used when copying a structure with issue cloning): validates permissions, target project, issue types, required fields, components, versions and options, then creates clones with optional link, attachments, sub-tasks, epic and parent handling, reporting localized errors and warnings with progress.

Keeps short-lived server-side state objects (for multi-step operations such as backup, restore, copy and migration wizards) under numeric ids. Each state belongs to the user who created it; only that user or a Jira admin may read, touch or remove it. States idle for 6 hours are expired by a background job every 30 minutes.

Integration with Jira Software (agile): detects the agile app and version, locates Epic Name, Epic Link and Sprint fields, the epic issue type and link type, resolves epics, lists boards and their filters/projects, formats sprint names with state, and checks rank, sprint and epic change permissions.

Bridge to Advanced Roadmaps (Portfolio): detects the Portfolio, Roadmaps and Team Management apps, loads shareable and all teams and a team by id, and validates setting an issue's parent with the app's own hierarchy rules, reaching its services reflectively.

Advanced Roadmaps hierarchy integration: gets children and parent of issues, validates and sets an issue's Roadmaps parent with permission and sub-task checks, recognises team and target start/end custom fields, and exposes teams. Used by the Roadmaps extender and grouper.
Chooses how to find Advanced Roadmaps parent/child relations: via issue links, the issue index, Jira 11 index, or JQL, automatically by Jira version unless overridden.

Integration with Tempo apps (Accounts, Teams, Timesheets, Planner): detects availability, reads an issue's account, teams and roles, searches accounts/teams/roles, totals worked and planned seconds, validates and sets accounts, and interprets Tempo events, reaching Tempo services reflectively.
Integration with the third-party Tree custom field app: when installed, extracts the display name of a tree field value.

Compatibility support for the 'Epic Sum Up' app: recognises its time custom field (converting seconds to formatted durations for the current user) and lists its progress/indicator custom field types that can only be rendered client-side.

Optional bridge to ScriptRunner Behaviours: for an issue, determines which fields Behaviours mark read-only so Structure's inline editing honours them. Works through reflection against different ScriptRunner versions and fails soft.

Supplies a shared bridge to Jira Service Management: reads and changes the customer request type of issues (with validation that target and source belong to the same service desk and compatible issue type), resolves portals and request types for display.
HTTP client to the vendor's app-support web service: posts JSON requests encrypted with an embedded RSA public key and decrypts responses, with configurable base URL and timeout.

Periodically (daily by default) reports license and installation facts for Structure and its registered extension apps to the vendor's app-support service, and records whether the vendor says each license is blocked; skipped in dev mode unless enabled.
Holds the vendor's X.509 certificate embedded in the plugin and verifies that other certificates are signed by it; used when validating signed license or support material.

Central registry of Structure extension modules declared by this and other plugins (item types, generators, effectors, effect providers, attribute loader providers, export renderers, synchronizers, S-JQL constraints, backup, calendar, performance log and integration-details providers). Tracks module enable/disable events and versions the lists.
Keeps a per-session in-memory clipboard forest so users can copy or cut rows and paste them into structures; idle clipboards expire.

Remembers each user's recently opened structures (most recent first, capped at 10 by default) in the user's settings, and returns the recent structures the user can still access, including the most recent accessible one used for auto-selecting a structure.
Sends and receives Structure's inter-node messages over Jira's cluster messaging on Data Center; does nothing on a single server.
Clears Structure's caches, either all caches or those of one user, locally or on all cluster nodes by broadcasting a message.

Formats dates and durations for display: named date styles (date-short, date-long, date-full, datetime-short, datetime-long, jira-date, jira-datetime) in the current user's locale, Jira time-tracking duration formatting and parsing, and calendar-time duration parsing.

Backs pickers in sharing and configuration dialogs: searches groups, project roles, projects, agile boards and unarchived versions of given projects by text, returning labelled result groups with highlighted matches and footers when results are truncated.
Collects statistics about cached forests (general and pinned caches): version, row count, unique items, item types and depth distribution, for the performance audit log.
Keeps a bounded in-memory log (default 400 entries) of recent forest recalculations: full or incremental, versions, timings and change summaries per generation step, for the performance audit log.

Collects attribute-loading performance metrics, keeps a ring buffer of slow requests and a record of attributes that failed to load (with last user, forest, row, item), and periodically snapshots statistics.
Keeps a bounded in-memory log of recent synchronizer runs with timings and reports which synchronizers are installed and enabled per structure, for the performance audit log.
Keeps bounded in-memory logs of recent effector preparation and application runs (what, for whom, status, times and counts) for the performance audit log.
Persists per-structure manual adjustments to an automated (generated) forest as a versioned serialized blob with optimistic concurrency and a per-structure size limit.
Manages manual adjustments to generated structures: whether they are enabled globally and per structure, who may make them, applying and deleting adjustments, and reporting usage statistics.
Short-lived per-user cache (about 60 s) of the set of rows or issues matching a query (JQL, S-JQL, text) within a forest, used by attributes that test query membership.

Parses a query of type 'sjql', 'jql' or 'text' (quick text search) into something that can be validated and executed against a forest, returning matching rows; JQL/text match the issues among the forest rows.

Checks the Atlassian Marketplace for newer versions of an installed app (Structure or its extensions) compatible with the current Jira build, caching the answer; used by the info popup to show 'update available'.
Version-specific adapter that reports whether attachments are enabled in Jira.

Listener for the Jira Cloud Migration Assistant (Connect and Forge paths). When a migration starts it finds the configuration matching the migration plan name (or migrates everything), backs up the selected structures, their views and Structure dashboard gadgets into zipped app-data chunks, uploads a table of contents and updates the configuration status.

Persists named cloud-migration configurations (scope) chosen by admins: name, status (draft, ready, running, done, failed), selected structure ids, selected extension keys, run time and last editor. Backs the 'Migrate to cloud' admin pages.
Collects all configured Structure dashboard gadgets (dashboard id, position, user preferences) whose structure is in the migration scope, for inclusion in cloud migration exports.
Renders a user as an HTML snippet (profile link, avatar, display name) for user-type attribute values in the grid.
Builds fast checks for whether a user belongs to a project role or a group for a batch of issues, used to filter restricted comments and worklogs in attributes.
Reads, in batches directly from Jira's database, the most recent comment of each issue that the user is allowed to see, for the 'last comment' attribute.

Implements what happens when a user drags an issue between groups of a field grouper (priority, components, versions, labels, assignee, reporter, status, sprint, custom fields): produces Jira update effects with notifications, or blocks moves for fields that cannot change.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Excel Field Provider
modules.purpose: Builds the Excel cell renderer for an exported Jira field column, or a summed time-aggregate field column. Issue keys become hyperlinks. Number, date, date-time, duration, URL, vote and watch fields get typed, right-aligned or linked cells. Other fields become rich text from their HTML value. Thumbnail fields are skipped. With aggregate=sum the sub-tree sum is exported.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Excel Joined and Icons Provider
modules.purpose: When a combined-fields ('joined') or 'icons' column is exported to Excel, splits it into one separate spreadsheet column per listed Jira field, each rendered the same way as a single field column.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Printable Field Provider
modules.purpose: Renders a Jira field column (or a summed time-aggregate field column) in the printable HTML export, using the field's HTML value. Long fields (links, labels, environment, description, custom fields) wrap over several lines. For user fields, the column's 'view' option is passed on.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Printable Joined Provider
modules.purpose: Renders a combined-fields ('joined') column in the printable export as one cell with the HTML values of all listed fields joined together. A column name written in braces is treated as an i18n key and translated.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Printable Icons Provider
modules.purpose: Renders an 'icons' column in the printable export as a cell of small icons for the chosen fields: issue type, priority, status, assignee, reporter and project. An unsupported field id or an empty field list is an error.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Main Column Provider
modules.purpose: Renders the main 'Summary' column for both export formats, using the aggregated summary attribute. In Excel the cell is indented by the row's depth in the hierarchy. In print it is a padded, wrapping cell. Rows whose item failed to load show a 'loading failed' text.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Progress Provider
modules.purpose: Renders the Progress column in exports by requesting the progress attribute with the column's settings. Excel gets a percentage cell. Print shows a progress bar, or percent text when the column is set to display percents.

modules.name: exportrenderer:WorkLogged Provider
modules.purpose: Renders the 'Work Logged' column in exports as a duration cell. It asks for the logged-time attribute with the column's period (a named preset or an explicit from/to range), time zone, and optional author, group or role filter. With aggregate=sum it exports the sub-tree sum. Without a valid period the column is skipped.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Attribute Column Provider
modules.purpose: Exports a generic 'attribute' column whose parameters carry an arbitrary attribute spec. The value is exported as HTML (rich text in Excel) when the attribute is HTML or can be converted to HTML, and as plain text otherwise. A column without an attribute is rejected.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Sequenial Index Column Provider
modules.purpose: Exports the sequence-number column: the hierarchical outline number of each row, such as 1.2.3.

modules.name: exportrenderer:ItemID Column Provider
modules.purpose: Exports the item-id column. Issues show their numeric issue id. Other items show their item identity, with the item type written in simplified form.

modules.name: exportrenderer:RowID Column Provider
modules.purpose: Exports the row-id column: the numeric forest row id of each exported row.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Formula Column Provider
modules.purpose: Exports Formula columns by evaluating the formula and its variables, or their sub-tree sum when aggregate=sum (arrays are summed first). The display format sets the cell type: number or percentage (rounded to 0-9 digits), date or date-time, duration (work or calendar time), wiki-rendered HTML, or wrapping text. The default header is the formula's first 15 characters.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Notes Column Provider
modules.purpose: Exports the Notes column: the per-structure text note stored for each item under the column's note name (default 'notes'), shown as wrapping text.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Time in Status Provider
modules.purpose: Exports the Time in Status column. It passes the column's status selection, reopen, target-status, current-status and calendar options to the time-in-status attribute. The cell is a duration (calendar time unless work time is chosen) or a plain number, depending on the display format. With aggregate=sum it exports the sub-tree sum.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Query Match Provider
modules.purpose: Exports the Query Match column. The printable export shows the match marker HTML. Excel shows 1/0. With aggregate=sum it shows the count of matching rows in the sub-tree. The header defaults to the query text if it is 40 characters or fewer, otherwise to a name based on the query type.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Comment Column Provider
modules.purpose: Exports the Last Comment column: the HTML of the latest comment the user can see on each issue. It is rich text in Excel and a wrapping cell in print.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Tempo Work Logged Provider
modules.purpose: When Tempo Timesheets is installed, exports the Tempo Work Logged column as a duration. It asks for the Tempo logged-time attribute for the column's date range, filtered by accounts, users, teams and billable. With aggregate=sum it exports the sub-tree sum. Without a date range the column is skipped.

modules.name: exportrenderer:Tempo Planned Time Provider
modules.purpose: When the Tempo Planner API is installed, exports the Tempo Time Planned column as a duration for the column's date range, filtered by users, teams and roles. With aggregate=sum it exports the sub-tree sum. Without a date range the column is skipped.

modules.name: itemtype:Structure
modules.purpose: Item type for a whole structure placed as an item (e.g. in lists of structures); resolved by structure id and visible only to users with view permission on that structure.

modules.name: itemtype:Issue
modules.purpose: Item type for Jira issues: resolves issues by id, applies Browse Projects permission, supports creating new issues and editing issues from the structure grid (fields, transitions), detects deleted issues and exposes issue fields to formulas.

modules.name: itemtype:Project
modules.purpose: Item type for Jira projects (by id), visible to users who can browse the project; exposes name, key, url, email, lead and description to formulas.

modules.name: itemtype:Version
modules.purpose: Item type for project versions (by id), visible with Browse Projects on the version's project; exposes project, name, description, archived/released flags, release and start dates; ordered by version sequence.

modules.name: itemtype:Version Name
modules.purpose: Item type representing a version name shared across projects (string id), used by the version-name grouper; always visible.

modules.name: itemtype:Label
modules.purpose: Item type for an issue label (string id, validated as a label of at most 255 characters); always visible; displays the label text.

modules.name: itemtype:Loop Marker
modules.purpose: Item type for the marker row inserted when generation would create a cycle; it refers to the row where the loop was detected and becomes dead when that row no longer exists.

modules.name: itemtype:Generator
modules.purpose: Item type for generator rows (inserters, extenders, groupers, sorters, filters); new generators are created from a module key and parameters, and copying a structure gives it its own generator copies.

modules.name: itemtype:User
modules.purpose: Item type for Jira users (by user key); always visible; exposes key, name, active flag, email and display name to formulas.

modules.name: itemtype:Folder
modules.purpose: Item type for folders: named containers created from the grid, renamed by users with edit permission on the owning structure, and copied when used in another structure; named folders can also be virtual (string id) as group headers.

modules.name: itemtype:Status
modules.purpose: Item type for Jira statuses (string id), always visible; exposes name, description, sequence and category; ordered by sequence.

modules.name: itemtype:Resolution
modules.purpose: Item type for Jira resolutions (string id), always visible; exposes name, description and sequence.

modules.name: itemtype:Issue Type
modules.purpose: Item type for Jira issue types (string id), always visible; exposes name, description, sequence and whether it is a sub-task type.

modules.name: itemtype:Priority
modules.purpose: Item type for Jira priorities (string id), always visible; ordered so that higher priorities sort first unless a dark feature reverses it.

modules.name: itemtype:Group
modules.purpose: Item type for Jira user groups (by group name); always visible; exposes the group name.

modules.name: itemtype:Option
modules.purpose: Item type for custom field options (by option id); exposes value, disabled flag, parent option and sequence; displays cascading text for child options.

modules.name: itemtype:Sprint
modules.purpose: Item type for Jira Software sprints (by sprint id), visible when the user can see the sprint; exposes name, dates, state, sequence, goal and board.

modules.name: itemtype:Account
modules.purpose: Item type for Tempo accounts (by numeric account id), used by the Tempo account grouper; always visible.

modules.name: itemtype:Project Component
modules.purpose: Item type for project components (by id), visible with Browse Projects on the component's project; exposes name, description and lead.

modules.name: itemtype:Missing Item
modules.purpose: Item type used for rows whose item can no longer be resolved; always treated as inaccessible and dead.

modules.name: itemtype:Customer Request Type
modules.purpose: Item type for Jira Service Management customer request types, visible when Service Management is available and the user can load the request type; exposes name, issue type, description and help text.

modules.name: itemtype:Effector
modules.purpose: Item type for effector rows placed in a structure; new effector instances are created from a module key and parameters and are copied per owning structure.

modules.name: itemtype:Memo
modules.purpose: Generic item type "Memo": structure-owned text notes created and edited in the grid, with optional color and icon, shown with a memo icon; values come from the generic item store and are exposed to formulas.

modules.name: itemtype:PlanningTask
modules.purpose: Generic item type "Planning task": structure-owned placeholder tasks with issue-like fields that can be created from a sample issue or task and later converted to real issues; visibility also honours per-field configuration.

modules.name: itemtype:Attachment
modules.purpose: Item type for issue attachments, visible with Browse Projects on the issue; exposes created, file size, file name and author.

modules.name: itemtype:Comment
modules.purpose: Item type for issue comments, visible with Browse Projects on the issue; exposes author, update author, created, updated and body.

modules.name: itemtype:Worklog
modules.purpose: Item type for issue work log entries, visible with Browse Projects on the issue; exposes author, dates, comment, start date and time spent.

modules.name: itemtype:IssueLink
modules.purpose: Item type for issue links, visible when the user can see both linked issues; exposes source, destination, sequence and link type.

modules.name: itemtype:IssueLinkType
modules.purpose: Item type for issue link types, always visible; exposes name, inward/outward descriptions, style and sub-task/system flags.

modules.name: itemtype:ChangeHistoryGroup
modules.purpose: Item type for an issue change history group (one change event), exposing author, time, the changed issue and its change items to formulas.
Item type for a single field change inside an issue change history group, exposing field, from/to values and texts, the group and whether it is incremental.
Item type for a change history record of a memo (generic item), exposing author, time, the changed memo and change items to formulas.
Item type for Insight/Assets objects, visible according to Insight permissions; exposes the object label and other fields to formulas.

modules.name: itemtype:RemoteLink
modules.purpose: Item type for remote issue links, visible when the user can see the issue; exposes source issue, title, url, application and status details.

modules.name: inserter:JQL
modules.purpose: Inserter "JQL Query": inserts issues matching a JQL query (up to a configurable limit, default 1000). Users may add only matching issues at the top level; moving or removing issues inside the result is blocked.

modules.name: inserter:Agile
modules.purpose: Inserter "Agile Board": inserts issues from a Jira Software board's filter, either only epics or only non-epic, non-sub-task issues; available only when boards are supported.

modules.name: inserter:Text
modules.purpose: Inserter "Text Query": inserts issues found by a text search (sorted by issue key descending, limited); add/move/remove rules are the same as for the JQL inserter.

modules.name: inserter:Sub-structure
modules.purpose: Inserter "Structure": inserts the contents of another structure (optionally a sub-tree from a given row, optionally with a given user's security), and passes edits made inside it through to the source structure when the user has edit or automate permission there.

modules.name: inserter:Recent Issues
modules.purpose: Unlisted inserter that inserts the issues the current user viewed recently (newest first), refreshed about once a minute; used for recent-issue search results.

modules.name: extender:Sub-tasks
modules.purpose: Extender "Sub-tasks": adds sub-tasks (optionally only selected sub-task types) under their parent issues. Moving a sub-task under another issue changes its parent; reordering changes sub-task order, subject to permissions and project rules.

modules.name: extender:Links
modules.purpose: Extender "Linked Issues": adds issues linked by a chosen link type and direction under each issue. Dropping an issue under another creates a link of that type; moving changes links; reordering is not supported.

modules.name: extender:Agile
modules.purpose: Extender "Stories under Epics": adds issues belonging to each epic under the epic. Placing issues under an epic adds them to it (sub-tasks and epics cannot be added); reordering is not supported.

modules.name: extender:Portfolio for JIRA children
modules.purpose: Extender for Advanced Roadmaps (Portfolio): adds issues whose Parent Link points to an issue under that issue; moving issues under another parent changes the Parent Link; reordering is not supported.

modules.name: grouper:Issue field
modules.purpose: Grouper "Issue Field": groups items by the value of a chosen field (project, type, status, priority, resolution, users, components, versions, labels, select/user/group custom fields, issue picker, Insight objects, request type). Moving items between groups updates the field (status via workflow transition) when allowed.

modules.name: grouper:Agile Sprint
modules.purpose: Grouper "Sprint": groups issues by sprint. Moving an issue to another sprint group changes its sprint, except into or out of closed sprints or to a board the issue does not belong to.

modules.name: grouper:Agile Epic
modules.purpose: Grouper "Epic": groups issues under their epic, optionally sorting epics by a rank field. Moving issues between epics changes epic membership; reordering epics changes their rank.

modules.name: grouper:Attribute
modules.purpose: Grouper "Attribute": groups items by the value of any attribute or formula, with a "No value" group; grouping is read-only (moving items does not change data). Offers a preset for grouping by sprint name across projects.

modules.name: grouper:Portfolio for JIRA parent
modules.purpose: Grouper that places issues under their Advanced Roadmaps (Portfolio) parent issue, with a "No parent" group; moving an issue to another group changes its Parent Link.

modules.name: grouper:Tempo Account
modules.purpose: Grouper "Tempo Account": groups issues by Tempo account (optionally including closed and archived accounts), with a "No account" group; moving issues between groups changes their account.

modules.name: grouper:Version Name
modules.purpose: Grouper "Version Name": groups issues and planning tasks by fix or affected version name across projects; moving items between groups changes their versions, blocked when the name maps to several versions in a project.

modules.name: grouper:Issue Links
modules.purpose: Grouper "Issue Links": groups each issue under the issue it is linked to by a chosen link type and direction; moving issues between groups changes the links.

modules.name: sorter:Attribute
modules.purpose: Sorter "Attribute": sorts sibling rows by an attribute or field value (ascending/descending, locale-aware text), keeping items without a value last; manual reordering within sorted rows is blocked.

modules.name: sorter:Agile Rank
modules.purpose: Sorter "Agile Rank": sorts issues by a Jira Software rank field; moving issues up or down in the structure changes their rank.

modules.name: sorter:Manual
modules.purpose: Sorter "Manual Reordering": remembers the order in which users manually arranged items under each parent (or group path) of generated content and reapplies it on regeneration.

modules.name: filter:Quick Filter
modules.purpose: Filter "Field" (quick filter): keeps issues whose chosen field has one of the selected values, optionally keeping non-issue rows.

modules.name: filter:Issue JQL
modules.purpose: Filter "JQL Query": keeps issues matching a JQL query, optionally keeping non-issue rows.

modules.name: filter:Item Text
modules.purpose: Filter "Text Query": keeps issues matching a text search and non-issue items whose key or summary match the text.

modules.name: filter:Item Attributes
modules.purpose: Filter "Attribute": keeps items whose attribute or formula value satisfies a chosen operator and value (including date and duration comparisons).

modules.name: filter:Number Attribute
modules.purpose: Unlisted filter that keeps rows whose numeric attribute value lies within an optional minimum and maximum; rows without a value are hidden.

modules.name: filter:S-JQL
modules.purpose: Filter "S-JQL Query": keeps rows matching a Structure query (S-JQL) evaluated over the generated forest, ignoring automation rows.

modules.name: filter:Item
modules.purpose: Unlisted filter that keeps only rows showing one specific item; used to "pin" a single item view of a structure.

modules.name: filter:Remove Inserter/Extender Duplicates
modules.purpose: Non-configurable filter "Remove Inserter/Extender Duplicates": hides top-level inserted items that already appear as extender-added children elsewhere; offered as a preset at level 1.

modules.name: filter:Sprint Filter
modules.purpose: Filter "Sprint": shows only sprint groups in selected states (active, future, closed, backlog/no sprint); available with Jira Software; preset "Hide Closed Sprints".

Serves the core 'item' attribute: the item object behind a row (issue, project, user, folder and so on). There are two variants: an extended-value form that may be cached, and a raw-object form that is never cached. Many other attributes depend on it.

Serves the localized 'displayable' text: a short description of any row item, used in messages and pickers. Examples are 'issue KEY: summary' (summary cut to 30 characters) and texts for new issues, folders, generators and effectors. It also covers projects, components, versions, issue constants, users, groups, labels, options, structures, loop markers, sprints, Tempo accounts, version names and generic items.

Serves the 'sum' aggregate attribute: for each row, totals a dependent number or duration attribute over the row and its sub-rows. Parameters choose a distinct sum (each item counted once) or a running total over all preceding rows ('preceding'); text-format dependents are summed as numbers.

Serves 'value-expand'. It wraps another attribute's value as a small JSON object: the value itself, an 'undefined' flag, or an 'error' with the formula error code (-1 if unknown). The client can then tell errors apart from empty values.

Serves core display attributes. 'summary' is the issue summary or the item's name (project, version, label, constant, component, option, group, structure, folder, sprint, Tempo account, request type, generic item, user marked when inactive, Insight object). It also serves 'description' (HTML and text), the extended summary of generators and effectors, and 'url' (browse, profile, Insight and generic item links).
Serves the core 'key' attribute: the issue or project key, the user name for users, a Structure-generated key for memos and planning tasks, and the object key for Insight (Assets) objects.
Serves the core 'done' boolean for issues. By default an issue is done when its status is in the Done status category. A dark feature switches the rule to 'the issue has a resolution'.

Serves the core 'editable' boolean for each row item. Issues are editable when Jira lets the current user edit them. Folders and generic items (memos and similar) are editable when the user can edit the owning structure. Generators and effectors are editable when the user may configure automation in it. The value depends on the viewing user.

Serves the core 'icon' HTML attribute for many item types. Examples: the issue-type icon for issues, the project avatar, the user avatar, status/type/priority icons, and version icons (released and archived variants). Generators, effectors, service desk request types, generic items and Insight objects get icons too. It also serves per-field icon attributes for the icons column and the printable export.

Serves basic issue attributes as native Jira objects, each with a trail so that changes to them invalidate dependent values. Covered are issue type, priority, project, status, assignee, reporter and creator. It also serves votes and watches counts, the issue id as text, and project, issue type and status ids.

Serves the HTML of any Jira issue field the user can see, as Jira's navigator shows it. Time-tracking and Epic Sum Up time fields show as durations. User fields use the user renderer and honour a 'view' param. The service desk request type shows as icon plus name. An 'excel' param gives plain text without links for spreadsheet export.

Serves sort-order values for standard issue fields, so Structure sorts the way Jira does. Keys sort by project key, then number. Status, resolution and priority use Jira's sequence, with priority reversed. Users and projects sort by name, components and labels by their names, and versions by sequence. Dates, time tracking, votes, watches and work ratio sort by raw value.
Serves the issue time-tracking values time spent, remaining estimate and original estimate as durations, converting Jira's seconds to milliseconds.

Serves issue dates as time values: created, updated and resolution date. It also serves the due date. A date-only value, the due date can be corrected to the viewing user's time zone (date-shifted spec) or returned unshifted, depending on the spec's date-shift flag.

Serves sort-order values for enumerated custom fields: select lists and cascading selects by option sequence, labels by first label, project pickers by project name, version pickers by project and version sequence, and user/group/Script Runner user fields by first name. It respects field-level security.

Serves typed values of Jira custom fields. Date fields give times, or localized text on request. Numeric fields give numbers, user fields give users, and most others give text. Some fields are handled specially: Agile sprint (comma-joined names), service desk request type, Tempo account and team, Advanced Roadmaps team and target dates, Epic Sum Up time, and Xray fields.

Serves 'progress' for the Progress column: how much of an issue and its sub-tree is done, 0 to 1. It can be based on time tracking, resolution, a percent field, or per-status or per-category percentages. Children can be weighted equally, by time or by a numeric field. The item itself may be included; resolved issues can count as complete.

Serves 'worklogged': the total time logged on an issue within a period. The period is a named preset relative to now, or an explicit from/to range in a given time zone. Work logs can optionally be limited to one author, one group or one project role.

For generator and effector rows, says whether a user added that automation to the saved structure, rather than it being produced by another generator. Transient rows are traced back to the original. The value is the automation's item identity, or undefined.
Serves an HTML tooltip hint for rows that have user-added generators or effectors among their children. It lists each one with its icon and summary under localized generator and effector headings.

Serves the internal '-non-unique-items' attribute used by distinct (de-duplicating) aggregates: for each subtree it reports which items occur more than once, either as per-item occurrence counts or with each repeated item's value; supports the 'preceding' mode and rejects the 'strict' mode.

For saved generators, serves the user the generator runs as, which is the owner of the structure that holds it. It is undefined for transient generators or when the structure cannot be accessed. Used to show a 'run as' user and its icon.
For generated rows, tells which kind of generator first produced the row, using the forest's generation history. The value is a one-letter code for extender, grouper, inserter or sorter.

For rows created by a generator, serves a small JSON object. It holds the creating generator's kind (sub-structure inserter, extender, grouper or inserter) and the generator's label, if any. Never cached.
For rows whose item is a Jira status, serves the extended summary as Jira's standard status lozenge HTML. It renders through Jira's issue-status template and returns an error when rendering fails.

Serves basic structural attributes for every row: 'count' (number of sub-rows, or only leaves with the 'leaves' parameter), 'depth' and 'level' (nesting depth), 'itemtype' (simplified item type of the row), 'itemid' (item identity as text) and 'issueid' (issue id, issue rows only).

Serves 'seq', the hierarchical outline number of each row (1, 1.1, 1.2.3 ...), worked out down the tree. Generators, effectors, loop markers and rows with special semantics get no number and do not use one up.
Serves the number of Jira issue links on an issue. The count can be limited to one link type and to inward or outward links. By default it counts all types in both directions.

Serves formula ('expr') attributes, the engine behind Formula columns. It parses the Structure expression language and binds named variables to other attribute specs. It pulls in any aggregations the formula uses and converts the result to the requested format, text by default. Automation and loop-marker rows are skipped. Caching follows the formula's dependence on user, locale, time zone and time.

Serves plain-text values of standard issue fields for use in formulas and text. It covers affects and fix versions, components, assignee, reporter, creator, description, environment, issue type, labels, priority, project, resolution, security level and status.

Serves item-based values of issue fields, such as versions, components, users, options and attachments. Values are single item references or lists of them, in the generic value format that formulas can follow.

Serves 'comments': the list of comment items on an issue that the current user may see. Visibility is checked in bulk against comment role and group restrictions, and the comments are pre-loaded so formulas can read them.

Serves 'worklogs': the list of work-log items on an issue that the current user may see. Visibility is checked in bulk against role and group restrictions, and the work logs are pre-loaded for formulas.
Serves 'history': the list of change-history group items for an issue. Histories are loaded in bulk for all requested issues and kept for formulas to read.
Serves 'parent': for a sub-task, the item identity of its parent issue. For other issues it is undefined.
Serves two Agile epic-link attributes: the epic an issue belongs to, and the list of issues in an epic. Both are computed in bulk from the Agile epic link and respect what the user can see.
Serves 'subtasks': the list of an issue's sub-task issues, computed in bulk from Jira's sub-task link.

For issues, returns the list of Jira issue links on the issue, as link items, keeping only links whose other end the user can see. 'issuelinkobjects' leaves out system link types and 'allissuelinkobjects' keeps them. Links are ordered as Jira orders them and loaded in bulk.

For issues, returns the list of remote (web) links as remote-link items. They are read in bulk from Jira's remote issue link table. A dark feature switches to loading them one issue at a time through Jira's remote link service.

Serves 'user-property': a Jira user property, returned as text, for the user named by another attribute that holds a user key. The property is stored under 'jira.meta.' plus the given property name. A dark feature can turn this off.

Serves 'formatted-number': another attribute's value turned into display text using display-format settings such as number, percentage, date/time, duration and rounding. It uses the user's locale and time zone. Formula columns use it.
