Serves per-structure item notes: the 'item property' attribute returns the text stored for an item in the current structure under a property name ('notes' for the Notes column). It is an error when there is no structure and undefined when nothing is stored.

Serves the 'max' and 'min' aggregates: the largest or smallest value of an attribute over a row and its sub-tree. Text is compared ignoring case. When the requested format differs from the one compared, it picks the row by the compared value and returns that row's value in the requested format.

Serves the internal attribute 'aggregation-value-path'. It links each row's value of an inner attribute to its parent row's value, so that parent and ancestor lookups can walk up the tree. It can include the invisible super-root and can skip the title row.

Serves 'aggregation-parent': an inner attribute's value taken from an ancestor row. A positive level counts down from the top of the tree. A negative level counts up from the row, so -1 is the parent. The title row can be skipped. Used by the formula parent and ancestor functions.

Serves two tree aggregations. 'aggregation-array' collects an inner attribute's values over a tree scope (sub-tree, ancestors, children, leaves and others). It can flatten, remove duplicates or empties, reverse, or limit to a level range. 'aggregation-join' joins the values into text with separators and brackets around children, writing '?' for missing values.

Serves the boolean 'manually-adjusted'. It is true for a row in a generated structure that a user has moved or changed by hand, contrary to what the generators produced. It is based on the forest's generation data.
Serves 'wiki-render': another attribute's text rendered to HTML with Jira's wiki-markup renderer. Formula columns use it for their wiki display format.

Supports 'version name' rows, which group versions that share a name across projects. It finds the issues under such a row and their projects, then derives the row's summary (the version name), icon (released or archived state, or 'mixed') and combined description from the matching versions.

Serves 'timeinstatus': how long an issue has spent in chosen statuses or status categories, worked out from status history. Options can count only time after a reopen, only stays ending in target statuses, or only the current status, and can use a working calendar. A stay still in progress counts up to now. Available as duration, number or HTML.

Serves 'status-category': the category of an issue's current status. It is given as the category id (number or order), its name (text), or a coloured lozenge (HTML). It is an error when the issue has no status or category.
Serves 'project-category': the name of the project category of an issue's project, or of a planning task's project. It is undefined when the project has no category.

Serves 'transition-date': when an issue first or (by default) last entered a given status, by id or name, or any status of a category. It also serves 'field-change-list': an issue's history of values for a field, as value-and-time entries starting from creation.

Serves 'query-match': whether each row matches a query (JQL, Structure's own query language, or text search) run over the current forest. The title row is never matched. The HTML form shows a check-circle icon for matches. An invalid or empty query gives undefined.
Serves 'comment': the last comment on an issue that the current user can see, loaded in bulk. As HTML it uses the renderer set for the comment field; as text it is the raw body.

For version items, serves 'version-start' and 'version-release' as times (optionally adjusted for time zone), formatted text or HTML. It also serves 'version-description' as text, and gives the plain-text description of version rows.

For sprint items, serves 'sprint-start' and 'sprint-end' as times (time-zone aware), formatted text or HTML. It also serves 'sprint-goal' as text, and gives the description of sprint rows as HTML and text.
For project items, serves 'project-lead': the display name of the project lead, as text or as escaped HTML.

When the Tempo apps are installed, serves two duration attributes. 'tempo-worklogged' is time logged in Tempo Timesheets in a date range, filtered by accounts, users, teams and billable. 'tempo-timeplanned' is time planned in Tempo Planner, filtered by users, teams and roles. Values are loaded in bulk and recalculated when Tempo access or worklog-view permissions change.

Serves field values for Structure's own items, memos and planning tasks. For any attribute that maps to a field Structure manages, it reads that field from the item. The value comes as text, HTML (users as links, with an Excel variant) or the field's own value type, with time-zone handling for date fields.
Serves the core attributes project, type, priority, reporter and assignee for memos and planning tasks, read from Structure's own copies of those fields on the item.
Serves 'history' for memos and planning tasks: the list of change-history record groups stored for the item, loaded in bulk from Structure's history store for these items.
For memos and planning tasks, works out 'creator', 'created' and 'updated' by replaying the item's history. The creator is available as a user key, a user item or user HTML.

modules.name: New Structure Template: Empty
modules.purpose: Create Structure wizard template "Empty Structure": creates a structure with no content.

modules.name: New Structure Template: Personal Backlog
modules.purpose: Wizard template "Personal Backlog Structure": builds a structure with folders/memos for issues assigned to, reported by and watched by the user (JQL inserters grouped by status) and a chosen set of tracking columns saved as a view.

modules.name: New Structure Template: Backlog
modules.purpose: Wizard template "Backlog Structure": inserts issues of selected projects and versions with a JQL inserter and groups them by a chosen field, epic or sprint, optionally allowing changes via Structure.

modules.name: New Structure Template: Agile
modules.purpose: Wizard template "Agile Structure": inserts epics from selected Agile boards, adds stories under epics and optionally sorts by rank, with options to allow epic and rank changes via Structure.

modules.name: Structure Query Constraint: folder
modules.purpose: S-JQL constraint folder(): matches folder rows, optionally only those whose name matches a text or /regex/ argument.

modules.name: Structure Query Constraint: memo
modules.purpose: S-JQL constraint memo(): matches memo rows, optionally filtered by text or /regex/ on the memo text.

modules.name: Structure Query Constraint: item
modules.purpose: S-JQL constraint item(type[, text]): matches rows whose item type matches the given type name (short or full, or * for any) and optionally whose summary matches a text query or /regex/.

modules.name: Structure Query Constraint: rowId
modules.purpose: S-JQL row id constraint (see contract notes for its name): takes one positive number and matches only the row with that row id.

modules.name: Structure Query Constraint: planningtask
modules.purpose: S-JQL constraint planningtask(): matches planning task rows, optionally filtered by text or /regex/ on the summary.
Adds a 'Jira instance information' section to the Structure performance audit log: Structure version, Jira version, Data Center node id (or cluster off) and the current time.

Adds a 'Structures' section to the performance audit log listing every structure with its owner, its synchronizers (module, parameters, user, enabled state), generator and effector rows with parameters and ancestor rows, and manual-adjustment status.
Adds a section listing every saved Jira filter whose JQL uses the structure() function (id, name, query) to the performance audit log.
Adds a 'Forest caches' section to the performance audit log describing cached forests in the general and pinned caches: version, row count, unique item count, item types and row counts per depth.
Adds a 'Syncs' section to the performance audit log with recent synchronizer runs (duration, start time, details) as recorded by the sync observer.
Adds a 'Forest changes updates' section to the performance audit log with recent full/incremental forest updates: forest, version range, status, changes and timings.

Adds an 'Attribute System' section to the performance audit log: the last attribute cache cleanup and recent slow attribute-loading requests, each with total time, start time, counters and nested requests.
Adds the item change tracker's state to the performance audit log (node id, node signature, thread count, pending event queue size) when the active tracker supports it.

Adds an 'Effect applications' section to the performance audit log listing recent effect application runs per forest: status (running, stopped, success, failed) and per-effect-provider time and count.
Adds an 'Effect preparations' section to the performance audit log listing recent effect preparation (preview) runs per forest with status and per-provider time and count.

Sets an issue's Assignee to a given user (or unassigns when empty). Skips the change when the user already matches; validates through Jira's normal issue update (permissions, field on screen), optionally without notifications, and records an undo effect restoring the previous assignee.
Sets an issue's Priority to a given priority id via a validated Jira issue update; no-op if already equal; produces an undo effect restoring the old priority.
Sets an issue's Description text via a validated Jira issue update; empty and missing text are treated as equal; undo restores the previous description.
Sets an issue's Environment text via a validated Jira issue update; no-op if unchanged; undo restores the previous text.
Sets an issue's Resolution field (by resolution id, or clears it) via a validated Jira issue update; undo restores the previous resolution.
Sets an issue's Summary via a validated Jira issue update; no-op if unchanged; undo restores the previous summary.
Sets or clears an issue's Due Date via a validated Jira issue update; values compared in Jira's date-picker format; undo restores the old date.
Sets an issue's Reporter to a given user via a validated Jira issue update; no-op when same user; undo restores the previous reporter.

Moves an issue to a target status by finding and executing a workflow transition from its current status (optionally only transitions without a screen, optionally setting a resolution), with or without notifications. Errors if no suitable transition exists; undo transitions back and restores the resolution.
Sets a cascading-select custom field on an issue to a given option (parent option, or parent plus child), or clears it, via a validated issue update; undo restores the previous option.
Sets a project-picker custom field on an issue to a given project (or clears it) via a validated issue update; undo restores the old project.

Sets a Script Runner single issue-picker custom field to a given issue (or clears it). Rejects fields that are not single issue pickers or that Script Runner reports as read-only; undo restores the previous linked issue.
Sets a single-select (or radio) custom field on an issue to a given option or clears it, via a validated issue update; undo restores the previous option.
Sets the Advanced Roadmaps (Portfolio) Team field of an issue to a given team or clears it; refused for sub-tasks. Undo restores the previous team.
Sets a single user-picker custom field on an issue to a given user or clears it, via a validated issue update; undo restores the previous user.
Sets a single group-picker custom field on an issue to a given group or clears it; rejects multi-group fields. Undo restores the previous group.

Sets a single version-picker custom field to a version or clears it. Refuses versions from another project and adding/removing archived versions (except when undoing). Undo restores the previous version.
Sets a text (single- or multi-line) custom field on an issue to a given string via a validated issue update; empty and missing are equal; undo restores the old text.
Sets a number custom field on an issue to a given number (or clears it); compares values by the field's stored string form; undo restores the old number.
Sets a date-picker custom field on an issue to a date or clears it; for the Advanced Roadmaps target start/end fields it applies a UTC shift when needed. Undo restores the previous date.
Sets a date-time custom field on an issue to a timestamp or clears it via a validated issue update; undo restores the previous value.
Adds, removes, replaces or sets the system Labels of an issue through Jira's label service, refusing when the Labels field is hidden on the edit screen. Undo reverses the change.

Adds, removes or sets versions in a multi-version custom field of an issue; rejects single-version fields, versions from another project, and changes involving archived versions (except on undo). Undo reverses it.
Adds, removes or sets an issue's Affects Version/s; versions must belong to the issue's project and archived versions cannot be added or removed except on undo. Undo reverses the change.
Adds, removes or sets an issue's Fix Version/s with the same project and archived-version rules as Affects Versions; used e.g. when moving issues between version groups. Undo reverses the change.
Adds, removes or sets an issue's Components; each component must belong to the issue's project. Undo reverses the change.
Adds, removes or sets options of a multi-select or multi-checkbox custom field on an issue; undo reverses the change.
Adds, removes or sets users in a multi-user-picker custom field on an issue; undo reverses the change.
Adds, removes or sets groups in a multi-group-picker custom field; rejects single-group fields. Undo reverses the change.
Adds, removes or sets labels in a labels-type custom field on an issue; undo reverses the change.
Adds, removes or sets Insight/Assets objects (by object key) in an Insight object custom field on an issue; unknown object keys are errors. Undo reverses the change.

Represents a warning instead of a change: always resolves to an error carrying a translated message (i18n key plus arguments) and the related items, so automation can report problems in the effect preview/log. Duplicate warnings are merged.

Test/diagnostic effect: waits a given number of milliseconds (default 100) when applied, for a given item, and produces an identical effect as its undo. Negative delays or missing item ids are errors.
Sets an issue's Original Estimate (time tracking) to a duration in milliseconds, formatted as a Jira duration, via a validated update; zero counts as empty. Undo restores the old estimate.
Sets an issue's Remaining Estimate (time tracking) to a duration in milliseconds via a validated update; undo restores the previous estimate.

Moves an issue into, out of, or between Jira Software sprints. Requires the Agile integration and sprint field, rank permission, non-closed source and target sprints, and optionally that both sprints share a board. Merged effects record conflicting sprints; undo moves the issue back.

Adds a comment with the given text to an issue as the current user (blank text is a no-op), validated by Jira's comment service. Its undo deletes the created comment; several effects for one issue keep the last one and record the others as conflicts.
Deletes a given issue comment if the current user may delete it; the undo re-adds a comment with the same body.

Sets one field of a Structure-native generic item (memo or planning task) to a value, after validating the update with that item's field accessor; no-op if equal. Undo restores the previous value; merged effects record conflicting values.

Converts an item between a Jira issue and a Structure planning task: depending on strategy it creates the target item with copied field values, places it in the structure where the source row was (moving children), and/or deletes the source item. Requires edit access to the structure.

modules.name: effector:Attribute
modules.purpose: Effector "Attribute to Field": writes an attribute or formula value into a chosen Jira field for issues in the structure (set, add or remove for multi-value fields), optionally limited by JQL and with or without email notifications.

modules.name: effector:Status Rollup
modules.purpose: Effector "Status Rollup": sets each parent issue's status to the earliest (in a configured order) status among its children, for selected projects and issue types, optionally setting a resolution, reporting warnings for unlisted or untransitionable issues.

modules.name: effector:Delay
modules.purpose: Test/diagnostic effector "Delay" that only waits for configured preview and apply durations in milliseconds.

modules.name: effector:Conversion
modules.purpose: Effector "Conversion": converts planning tasks in the structure (all or selected ones) into real Jira issues, optionally keeping the planning task row instead of replacing it.
Built-in calendar provider offering two calendars: a default round-the-clock calendar (id 0) and a work calendar (id 1) of weekdays 9:00-17:00, used by duration calculations in formulas.

modules.name: web-resource: Gadget and Macro Visibility Observer
modules.purpose: Observes when the structure container inside a gadget or macro becomes visible.

modules.name: web-resource:Gadget Resources without Dependencies
modules.purpose: Structure gadget code and styles without dependencies: initialization, configuration form, remote gadget extension for subscriptions.

modules.name: web-resource:Gadget Resources
modules.purpose: Complete resource set for the Structure dashboard gadget.

modules.name: web-resource:Macro Resources
modules.purpose: Resources for the external (embeddable) Structure gadget page used in Confluence macros.

modules.name: gadget:Structure
modules.purpose: Jira dashboard gadget 'Structure' that shows a chosen structure (or a filter/query) in a compact structure widget, with selectable view, number of rows, custom title, optional edits and separate maximized-view settings. Loads the gadget resources plus the structure.widget context so extension apps can add their parts.

modules.name: web-resource:CFD Gadget Resources without Dependencies
modules.purpose: Cumulative flow diagram gadget code, chart and templates without dependencies.

modules.name: web-resource:CFD Gadget Resources
modules.purpose: Complete resource set for the Cumulative Flow Diagram gadget.

modules.name: gadget:Cumulative Flow Diagram
modules.purpose: Jira dashboard gadget 'Cumulative Flow Diagram' that charts work items of a scope structure over time and forecasts completion using a training structure and simulation, with options for issue types, team attribute, target date, appearance/start/completion attributes and adjustments.

modules.name: jql-function:structure()
modules.purpose: JQL function structure(): returns issues in a structure. With no arguments uses the default structure; one argument is a structure name/id or an S-JQL query; two arguments are structure and S-JQL query. Reports errors for unknown, ambiguous or blocked structures.

modules.name: servlet:Excel Export
modules.purpose: Servlet that exports a structure as an Excel workbook. Takes a forest specification (JSON), view id or view spec, expansion state, client-side filter and an xlsx flag; builds a workbook with the view's columns and returns it as an attachment (.xls or .xlsx). Maps failures to 400/403/404/500, or 503 when automation failed, and counts the user as active.

modules.name: activity-streams-provider:Structure
modules.purpose: Activity Streams provider "Structure": publishes structure change history (items added, copied, moved, removed) to Jira activity streams, with filter options for structure, ancestor item and synchronizer.

modules.name: Issue Matches Structure Query
modules.purpose: Workflow condition "Issue Matches Structure Query" (disabled by default): allows a transition only if the issue, in the default or a chosen structure, matches an S-JQL query evaluated as the project lead or a chosen user; issues not in the structure pass only if allowed.

modules.name: Issue Matches Structure Query
modules.purpose: Workflow validator "Issue Matches Structure Query": blocks a transition with an explanatory message unless the issue matches an S-JQL query in the default or a chosen structure, evaluated as the project lead or a chosen user.

Contributes workflow usage statistics: scans active Jira workflows for Structure's workflow condition and validator and counts their configurations (structure type default/manual/containing, JQL in the query, unstructured allowed or blocked, run as project lead or user).

Declares the plugin's Active Objects database schema (39 tables) holding all persistent Structure data: structures, forests and change log, rows, generators, item types, folders, generic items and their history, views, favorites, properties, history, sync instances/events/audit, effectors and effect records, orderings, manual adjustments, notes, saved columns and process state.
First plugin upgrade task ('upgrade prepare'); performs no data changes itself, but when the JVM system property for reset is set it clears the stored build number so all upgrade tasks re-run.
Developer-mode-only entry 'View as JSON' in the Structure Board's export menu, linking to the forest REST resource for the current forest specification.

modules.name: Structure Index Monitor
modules.purpose: Locked internal custom field type "Structure Index Monitor" that stores no data; a single global field of this type is created automatically so that its indexer is invoked whenever Jira reindexes an issue, letting Structure notice reindexing (used on Data Center).

modules.name: Structure Index Monitor Searcher
modules.purpose: Searcher paired with the Structure Index Monitor field; its indexer hook reports every issue reindex to Structure's item change tracking. Not intended for users to search with.
Tracks Jira issue, project and full reindexes (fed by the index monitor field and reindex events) and notifies internal listeners so item tracking and synchronizers can react to reindexed issues.

Reads issue links in bulk straight from Jira's entity store for many issues at once, by direction and optional link type, with optional ordering, batching large id lists; used by link-based generators and synchronizers.
Ensures that a global, locked, managed custom field named 'Structure Index Monitor' exists (creating or recreating it under a cluster lock) so the plugin is notified whenever Jira reindexes an issue.
Detects custom fields of type 'STAGIL Assets relation' (cached per field) so Structure can treat them specially.

Classifies issue link types: sub-task and epic link types are internal; other system link types are 'hidden' and offered to users only when the hidden-links feature flag is on. Used where link types are listed or followed.

Shared support for link-based generators: lists visible and hidden link types, validates link type and direction parameters on generator forms, builds summaries, and creates or removes Jira issue links when users move rows under link extenders and groupers.
Decides whether synchronizer features are shown in the UI: true if the synchronizers feature flag is on or at least one synchronizer is installed (checked once).

Translates non-issue Jira and third-party events into item changes: versions, projects, components, issue types, priorities, archived issues, permissions, agile sprints and boards, Tempo, Insight/Assets objects and Xray test runs; custom field changes clear all caches.

Reacts to user, group membership, project role, permission scheme, issue security scheme, user preference/profile/avatar and anonymization events by clearing permission and per-user caches (cluster-wide) and recording user or group changes.

Participates in Jira user anonymization and ownership transfer for structures: lists and removes permission rules that name the user, lists and deletes the user's private (unshared) structures, and lists and transfers ownership of the user's shared structures to another user, reporting failures per structure.

Participates in Jira user anonymization and ownership transfer for views: deletes the user's private views and transfers ownership of the user's shared views to another user, reporting failures per view.
When a structure is deleted, removes its synchronizers, manual adjustments, structure properties and item properties (notes).

Provides date and date-time formatting for attribute values in either the viewing user's or the system time zone and locale, plus helpers that shift date-only field values between time zones so dates display on the correct day.

Sends HTML/text emails rendered from the plugin's email templates to Jira users (asynchronously or immediately), adding base URL and the Structure logo; reports whether outgoing mail is configured. Used for sync error/cycle notices and shared perspective notifications.

Emails a link to a shared perspective to chosen users with an optional message; if the sender administers the structure and may browse users, it first grants the recipients view permission on that structure.

Helper for generic attribute values (number, string, boolean, item reference, list, map): dispatches on value kind and rewrites an attribute request for a custom field of the Epic Link type into the epic attribute, then asks for the value in a generic format. Used by formulas, generic item fields and effectors.

Registry describing how each Jira system field and supported custom field type can be read, parsed from text and written by effects (users, priority, status, resolution, versions, components, labels, sprints, options, groups, teams, etc.), with localized errors for unknown values.
Finds a Jira custom field id by name (case- and space-insensitive, preferring exact matches), optionally restricted to fields in scope for an issue's project and type; results are cached.

Stores administrator-defined help content for the Structure welcome/help screen (title, wiki content, list of contact users) as JSON in a plugin property, returns it with contact user details, and reports whether help tips are defined to statistics.

Builds the user representation used in REST responses (key, name, display name, avatar URL, profile link), with special handling for anonymous users and inactive users, and for permission subjects and gadgets.
Renders wiki markup to HTML (and to plain text) using Jira's wiki renderer, for content such as help texts and memos.

Provides searchable option lists for Jira fields (project, status, issue type, versions, priority, users, labels, components, resolution, custom field options, cascading options, groups) and builds JQL for chosen options; serves the issue-field options REST endpoint and the field filter.
Finds Jira users by exact display name across user directories, with a short-lived bounded cache; used by formula functions that resolve user names.

Stores saved (reusable) column definitions in the database: name, description, column type, owner (null for global columns) and JSON parameters. Creates, updates, deletes, restores with a fixed id, and promotes user columns to global; caches columns per owner and per id and drops caches on change.

Read-only built-in saved column list 'bundled' of ready formula columns: WSJF (Basic, Tempo, SAFe), Total Work Ratio (points/time), bug-fix percentage (time/count), Total Underestimation, Due In, Time to Resolve and Time Since Last Update, adapting to the story points field.

The 'stored' saved-column source: exposes two lists, 'global' (shared) and 'user' (personal, hidden for anonymous users). Enforces that users only read and edit their own personal columns, that global columns are managed only by users holding the manage-global-saved-columns permission, and that columns may move to global but never back; supports backup export (owner) and restore.

Registry of saved-column sources (the bundled read-only source and the user-stored source), looked up by source id. When a view specification is loaded, it replaces each column that references a saved column with that column's current type and parameters, removes columns whose saved column no longer exists, and strips the reference from locally modified copies the user cannot read.

Shared toolkit for effect providers that write issue field values: identifies fields, builds update-issue effects with undo, compares old and new values, merges conflicting grouped effects and renders effect descriptions as HTML with conflict warnings.
Records the largest forest size updated within each statistics period and reports it, bucketed by size, to usage statistics.

Stores named Notes columns ('notes') that can be shared across structures: create, rename, archive, list and restore. Each note has a permission scheme (typically bound to a structure) which governs who may create or edit it; names are trimmed, non-blank and at most 190 characters.

Defines the field value types Structure supports (user, multi-user, group, date, date-time, text, multi-line text, number, duration, project, issue type, priority, version(s), components, labels, sprint, single/multi option) with storage conversion, HTML view and edit rendering and validation, and maps Jira custom field type keys to them.

Provides the catalogue of Jira fields that Structure can read and write uniformly: a fixed set of system fields (summary, description, assignee, due date, estimates, time spent, environment, reporter, priority, issue type, project, labels, versions, components) plus supported custom fields, with localized names and renderer info; refreshed every minute. Used by planning tasks, memos, groupers and effectors.

Parses stored permission scheme specs used by notes: a structure-bound scheme (JSON with structure id; edit follows structure access), basic levels ('none', 'view', ...) and the built-in default-note scheme, and checks a user's permission with readable denial reasons.

Backs the 'Manage structures' page data: lists all, favourite and recent structures (rate-limited searching), and enriches them with owner, permissions, last-used time, manual adjustments, synchronizers, effector counts, add-on details, running copy processes and problems.

Backs the structure REST resource: get one structure, list structures for a user (default/project/recent ordering, anchor issue), search, favourite toggling, mark as recent, quick transformations per structure, description visibility, and create/update/delete structures including owner change.

Provides option lists for pickers when editing planning tasks and similar fields: projects, issue types, priorities, versions, components, sprints, users, groups and custom-field options, with filters (exclude sub-tasks/inactive, can create issues, assignable, project enabled for Structure), grouping and recents.

Shared helpers for option pickers: renders the edit HTML of single/multi option pickers from a server template and provides short-lived per-key caches used by the recents and sprint-board suggestion services.
Returns, per user and history type, the Jira user-history entries (recently viewed projects, etc.) so pickers can show recent choices first; cached briefly and cleared per user.
For a project and user, returns the agile boards relevant to that project, used to suggest sprints in pickers; cached briefly.
Searches available notes by name for the note picker, grouping results into the default note, notes already used in the given structure, and other notes, with a result limit.

Decides which fields a generic item has and validates field updates. Memos expose a fixed small set (summary, description, assignee, due date, original/remaining estimate, time spent); planning tasks mirror the field configuration of their Jira project and issue type, inject required fields, and supply option lists for pickers.

Computes, per project, issue type and user, whether a Jira field is visible, required or editable for planning tasks, following the Jira field configuration and the create-issue screen; project and issue type are always required, time-tracking fields map to Jira's time tracking field. Also checks project visibility; results are cached briefly.
Shared logic for generic items (memos, planning tasks): exposes key, name, summary, description, created, updated, creator and history to formulas, parses edits, and builds item keys and board links.

Builds field-level read views and update builders over generic items (memos, planning tasks), combining the stored item with the per-type field configuration and the structure field definitions, including agile (sprint) fields. Used by the memo and planning-task managers.

Copies an issue's project, issue type and visible field values into a planning task (or computes the list of field updates), mapping Jira field values to Structure fields; used when converting issues to planning tasks.

Supplies a shared, lazily-resolved bridge to the Insight/Assets app (if installed) used to load objects, their attributes, status names, objects selectable in Insight custom fields, and permission checks.

Converts Insight/Assets object attribute values into formula values: dates shifted to the user's time zone, date-times as timestamps, text areas stripped of HTML, and referenced objects, users, groups, versions and projects turned into item references; statuses become names.
Renders a full Jira-style login page for the external Structure gadget when an anonymous viewer needs to sign in, using Jira login properties and the plugin's gadget login template.

Runs expensive REST requests (poll, forest, item, value, effect and synchronizer calls) as background jobs bound to a configurable timeout, so a client can retry and pick up the same job's result instead of blocking.
Version-specific adapter that builds static URLs for plugin resources and the static resource prefix (relative or absolute).
Answers whether the current user may see Structure UI: the app must have a license and Structure must be enabled for the user; drives the issue-page decorator condition.
Answers whether Structure should appear on the issue page, controlled by a feature flag; drives the issue-page web resources condition.
Version-specific adapter to require web resources and contexts on the current page, read required resources and put page metadata.
Adapts servlet request/response/session objects of either servlet API generation (javax for Jira 9-10, jakarta for Jira 11+) to a common form used by plugin code.
Version-specific adapter for getting, setting, caching and clearing Jira's Velocity request context (base URL info) for rendering outside normal requests.
Version-specific adapter exposing the current HTTP request and response in the common bridged form.
Version-specific adapter exposing the current web action's request and response in the common bridged form.
Version-specific adapter to print and parse ISO/XML date-time strings.
Plugs into Jira's user anonymization/ownership transfer: lists and transfers ownership of structures, views and synchronizers owned by a user to another user.
Plugs into Jira's user anonymization: when a user key changes, updates the user key stored in Structure history, statistics, effector processes and synchronizer records.
Plugs into Jira's user anonymization: lists and deletes a user's Structure personal data, i.e. private structures and views they own, their permission rules and favorite marks.

Allows Jira's restricted Velocity engine to call the listed read-only getters from Structure's templates for the create-structure wizard pages: template choices, step state, step titles and buttons, and the step-specific fields of the backlog, personal backlog and agile templates.

Allows Jira's restricted Velocity engine to call the listed read-only getters from Structure's templates for the Structure Board page, the printable export page (header/data row HTML, warnings, depths), the search-data page, the cache-clearing page and the keyboard shortcuts page.

Allows Jira's restricted Velocity engine to call the listed read-only getters from Structure's templates for the generator edit dialog and the generator forms (sub-task types, supported fields, Agile rank fields and boards, link types and directions).

Allows Jira's restricted Velocity engine to call the listed read-only getters from Structure's templates for the effector edit dialog and forms, effector process start/progress/preview/result pages, the effector audit page and the processes list.

Allows Jira's restricted Velocity engine to call the listed read-only getters from Structure's templates for Manage Structures and related pages: structure details and permissions, edit, archive, delete, remove adjustments, views management and copy structure (with copy progress and statistics).

Allows Jira's restricted Velocity engine to call the listed read-only getters from Structure's templates for synchronizer pages: list, create, edit, resync, import/export and the synchronizer-specific forms (links, Agile, status rollup, sub-tasks).

Allows Jira's restricted Velocity engine to call the listed read-only getters from Structure's templates for the administration pages: backup, restore, migrate preview, configuration, defaults, license details, maintenance, project settings, setup guide, support, help editor, audit logs and troubleshooting.

Allows Jira's restricted Velocity engine to call the listed read-only getters from Structure's templates for the welcome page and the help dialog: images, help title/content/contacts, licensing state and which companion apps are installed.

Allows Jira's restricted Velocity engine to call the listed read-only getters from Structure's templates for all pages: shared action helpers (static resource prefix, admin check, self link, user and permission formatting, resource requiring), structure and user info objects, field info and rendering helpers.

Allows Jira's restricted Velocity engine to call the listed read-only getters from Structure's templates for remaining pages: issue-page time tracking section, external gadget and its login page, cloud migration configurations, structure field options, project tab links, background process status and workflow checker forms.
